cultivar: Local population bushes and other suitable varieties
processing: Fully oxidised black tea, made in two lines: gongfu strips and CTC broken tea.
harvest_season: The traditional tea it descends from used one bud and one leaf picked around Qingming; spring lots are the ones to look for.
appearance_dry: Fine tight strips with many tips and an even red tone, or, in CTC, firm granules showing golden tips.
appearance_wet: Tender, even leaf, red and bright.
taste_profile: Gongfu lots are mellow and smooth with a fresh, tender aroma and natural floral notes; CTC is stronger and brisker.

brewing.notes: This suits the gongfu strips. Brew CTC Western-style with short steeps, about two minutes, and add milk if you like.

vintage_note: Sold as a current-year black tea, with spring gongfu lots at the top. There is no ageing market to speak of; look for the geographical indication mark and drink it within a couple of years.
description:
Pu'an Hong is the protected black tea of Pu'an County in southwest Guizhou. The area averages about 1,400 metres, with mild winters and summers, and the county also markets itself on its old tea trees.

It comes in two very different forms. Gongfu strips are the loose-leaf drinker's tea, while CTC granules are made for strength and body.

The gongfu version is smooth and sweet, with a fresh, tender aroma. Use water slightly off the boil and short steeps, and it will hold up for several rounds. The CTC is stronger and sits better with milk.

The protected area covers 12 towns and subdistricts in the county, so ask for the mark if origin matters. Asking which of the two forms you are getting is just as useful.
history:
Local accounts link the tea to Funiang tea, a traditional tea of the Buyi people, picked around Qingming and offered to honoured guests, and date that craft to the Ming. That dating comes from promotional writing and should be read as such.

The more firmly documented part is recent. The brand was first registered as Funiang black tea and renamed Pu'an Hong in May 2015, and in July 2016 the national quality authority granted geographical indication protection.
